status.heading: Personal status
status.intro: Your own status per entry (status, notes, gut feeling), chosen criteria, areas, reference point and budget can live in a private GitHub repository of yours. Paste a GitHub token that can read only that repository; this site then reads your status file and shows it on top of the public data. Read-only: nothing is ever written.
status.remember: Remember the token on this device
status.remember_warning: By default the token stays in this tab's memory only and is gone when you close or reload it. If you choose to remember it, it is stored in this browser's local storage for this site. Every *.github.io project site of the same GitHub owner shares that storage, so only do this on your own device and with a token limited to your status repository. The token is only ever sent to api.github.com.
status.setup.1: Create a private repository for your status, and in it a file such as my.status.yaml (see the example in this site's repository: the default status file).
status.setup.2: On GitHub: Settings → Developer settings → Fine-grained personal access tokens → Generate new token.
status.setup.3: Repository access: Only select repositories → just your status repository. Permissions: Contents read-only (Metadata read-only is added automatically). Set an expiry date.
status.setup.4: Paste the token above. A token that can read more than one private repository is refused.
